videos.title: A tour of the parent area

steps.say: Welcome to the parent area. It is a grown-ups-only space, behind a PIN that only you know.
Overview shows how each child is doing this week: time, questions answered and how many were right on the first try.
Under each child you can see how every subject is going, and tap Full report for the details.
Reports has charts, strengths, and a table of every unit.
Children is where you add or edit your children, and Settings lets you tune each child's experience.
Account is for signing in, syncing between devices, your PIN and the read-aloud voice.
To add a child, open the Children tab.
Tap Add a child.
Type a first name or nickname. That is all we keep. No last names, photos or free text from children.
Pick their grade, and the province or state they follow, so practice matches their school curriculum.
Save, and the new child shows up with their own settings and reports. You can add up to five children.
Each child has their own settings. Open Settings and pick the child at the top.
The daily goal sets how many minutes of learning fill their progress bar on the home screen.
Subjects lets you choose what shows up in lessons, Adventure and the Daily Challenge. French is optional and off by default.
Arcade games are earned with learning time. You can change the ratio, allow free play, or turn games off.
Changes save automatically and sync to your other devices.
Reports shows what your child has practised. Choose 7, 14, 30 or 90 days.
Is it working compares today with the past, so you can see which units moved up a level.
The charts show minutes per day and how many answers were right on the first try. Every chart has a table view.
Strengths and Worth practising point to what to celebrate and what to practise next.
Every unit lists each level. These reflect practice, not a report-card mark. Your child's teacher decides proficiency.
On Overview you can set a weekly goal for how many days your child practises.
Send a kind note from a short list. It shows once on their home screen. We never send push messages to children.
Focus picks one unit, like a test coming up, and it comes up more in Adventure.
A goal plan spreads a set of units over the weeks, to get ready for next grade or catch up.
A reward is something small you promise for the coins they earn by learning. You give it yourself. Coins are never spent.
Some children find motion, noise or time pressure hard. In Settings, Calm and focus can help.
One switch turns on calm motion, gentle sounds, hidden timers, trophy pop-ups after the lesson and shorter sessions. Scoring stays the same.
Customize calm mode lets you set each one separately.
Reading and sound has read-aloud, sound choices, roomy text and high contrast.
Everything here changes presentation only, so your child's progress is always scored the same way.
Practice sheet makes a printable page from your child's trickiest units. Find it in Reports.
There are ten questions, chosen at the right level, with a separate page for the answer key.
Tap New questions for a fresh sheet any time, then print it for the table or the car ride.
Account is where you sign in, so progress is backed up and synced between tablets, phones and computers.
Your parent PIN keeps this area grown-ups only. It is saved on this device.
Pick the read-aloud voice, hear a sample, and see what we store. You can export or delete everything at any time.
